title: -ból/-ből áll: What Is the Coat of Arms Made Of?

sections.content: To say WHAT something is built from — what its parts or components are — you combine the *-ból/-ből* ending (which you already know in its "out of, from" sense, e.g. *kimegyek a szobából*, I go out of the room) with the verb *áll*. This structure is ideal for describing the flag and the coat of arms, which are built from precisely defined parts.

sections.title: The -ból/-ből áll pattern
rows: consists of a shield and a crown

items.spanish: A zászló három sávból áll: pirosból, fehérből és zöldből.
items.english: The flag consists of three stripes: red, white and green.

items.spanish: A címer egy pajzsból és egy fölötte lebegő koronából áll.
items.english: The coat of arms consists of a shield and a crown floating above it.
The country consists of nineteen counties.

sections.content: *áll* here means "to consist", not "to stand" — but it's the same verb, and the *-ból/-ből* on the material or the parts is exactly the case ending you already use for "out of" or "from". After a number, the noun stays singular in Hungarian (*három sávból*, not *sávokból*), so *három sávból áll* is correct, not *három sávokból áll*.
